screens.prompt: In B9, count the products whose name starts with "Widget" using one wildcard.

hints.syntax: =COUNTIF(A2:A8,"Widget*"): the pattern sits inside the quotes.
hints.func-countif: The column is text, so the count has to come from matches rather than numbers.
hints.require-ref: Match the pattern against the product column itself, not against the answer cell.
hints.value: The star covers the rest of each name, so all four Widget rows count.
hints.error: Without quotes the pattern is read as a name, and the cell shows #NAME?.

reject.why: COUNT counts numbers, and this column holds text, so it answers 0
no row is exactly "Widget", so the answer is 0 rather than 4
an exact name instead of a pattern, so only one row counts
the range starts on row 3, so the first Widget is never counted
division by zero, so the cell holds #DIV/0!
the missing comma leaves COUNTIF with a single argument
every name counts, including the two Gadgets and the Gizmo — 7

screens.prompt: In B9, count the products whose name ends with "B".

hints.syntax: =COUNTIF(A2:A8,"*B"): the star goes in front of the letter.
hints.func-countif: Matching part of a name is still a counting question, not a lookup.
hints.require-ref: Point the pattern at column A, where the names live.
hints.value: Three names end in B: Widget B, Gizmo B and Gadget B.
hints.error: A star on the other end, B*, matches names beginning with B and counts 0 here.

reject.why: the star points the other way, so it looks for names that begin with B and finds none
an exact match on a single letter, so nothing is counted
the wrong ending, which counts the two A names instead of the three B names
the range starts on row 3, so Widget B in row 2 is left out
division by zero, so the cell holds #DIV/0!
a typed 2 is not a count of the names

docs.syntax: =COUNTIF(range, "pattern*") counts the names that match; * stands for any run of characters and ? for exactly one
docs.explain:
COUNTIF criteria accept two wildcards, and either one turns an exact match into a pattern. The star stands for any run of characters, including none, so Widget* covers Widget A, Widget B, Widget C and Widget D. The question mark stands for exactly one character, so Gadget? misses Gadget B because of the space.

The wildcards sit inside the quotes with the rest of the pattern. Widget* returns 4 here. Move the star to the front and *B returns 3, the three names ending in B: Widget B, Gizmo B and Gadget B.

Without a wildcard the criterion is the whole cell, so Widget on its own returns 0 because no cell holds that word. A star on the wrong end counts another set of rows and still returns a number that looks plausible.

errors.text: A pattern typed without quotes, as in Widget*, is read as a name that does not exist.
An exact criterion that no cell holds, such as Widget on its own, returns 0 without a warning.
A star on the wrong end counts another set of rows and still returns a plausible number.

docs.atWork: Counting every product in one family, and counting records that share a code prefix or suffix.
docs.outcome: Count partial matches on text instead of listing every exact value that qualifies.
docs.teaches: COUNTIF with * and ? wildcards, and where the star has to sit
docs.dataset: Product list with mixed names and unit quantities

seo.title: COUNTIF with wildcards in Excel
seo.description: The star matches any run of characters and the question mark matches one. A star on the wrong end of the pattern silently counts a different set of rows.
